prompt: State the mathematical relationship between the mean-square speed in one direction <c_x^2> and the three-dimensional mean-square speed <c^2>, and state the assumption of the kinetic theory of gases that justifies this relationship.

mark_scheme.criterion: States that molecular motion is random (or there is no preferred direction of motion, so <c_x^2> = <c_y^2> = <c_z^2>).

hints: Write Pythagoras' theorem for velocity components: <c^2> = <c_x^2> + <c_y^2> + <c_z^2>.
What does randomness imply about the symmetry between x, y, and z directions?
solution:
Relationship: <c_x^2> = (1/3) <c^2> (or <c^2> = 3 <c_x^2>).
Justifying assumption: The motion of the molecules is completely random with no preferred direction of travel in space, so the mean-square speeds along all three Cartesian axes are equal: <c_x^2> = <c_y^2> = <c_z^2>.
teacher_walkthrough: Explain that the kinetic theory assumption of random motion guarantees equal distribution across all three axes.
Award 1 mark for the formula and 1 mark for stating random motion / no preferred direction.
